title: The interviewer's verdict on the album
summary: Davenport asks what the interviewer thought; he calls it the best he has heard Wallace play, praising the team understanding.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: What do you think people have that ready for me?
Well when he finishes it, I'll make him do all the work. I'll see what I can do. And maybe Chitty and Ralph can help out. We can all pitch in.
From what you heard, what did you think of the album? Just bring this. Okay.

No, I think it's marvelous. It's the best I've ever heard you play. And I really mean that. I'm talking, honestly I think that's the best thing I've ever heard Wallace do. Because I think he sounds comfortable with those cats. They understand what you're doing and you understand what they're doing. And that's what makes the teamwork. And that's what makes for good music for me. I don't care whether it's complicated or simple or what. You've got to understand what each other's doing.
